summary:
A 96-wide row of eight 12×14 plots facing a gravel lane, with a lantern post on each plot line. Four small pier-raised houses (a front-gable shotgun, a side-gable saddlebag duplex with a central chimney, a hall-and-parlour with an end chimney, and a mirrored shotgun) each have their own wood and tin colour and a porch on the lane. They are followed by a fenced kitchen garden, a chicken coop with its run, a well yard with a shade tree, and a false-front company store. Together they read as a cotton-mill village. One 96x19 row of eight 12-wide modules along a gravel lane: a shotgun house, a saddlebag duplex, a hall-and-parlour cottage, a mirrored shotgun variant, a kitchen garden, a chicken coop, a well yard and a false-front company store. Each has its own wood, roof tin, brick or stone piers, porch and brick chimney with a signal campfire; side columns are fences so plots tile.
elements.md and plan.md (PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS, PARTS, CHECKLIST, NOTES) are written. Six trade-cut parts.

Shell: parts/shell.mjs now builds the shell of plots 0-3 (piers, skirting, decks, walls, gable fills, partitions), the coop and the store body with false front. Every opening and chimney cell is left air. make.sh produces a whole build.nbt with no refused writes or off-palette blocks.
polish: Store back gable triangle (z 17, above y 7) is not built; the roof part must close it.
Plot 1 walls get their battens from local code, not batten_wall (it can't leave openings).
Crawlspaces inside the piers are filled with coarse_dirt at y 1 so nothing spawns under the floors.
Elements ticks in elements.md and the fittings (doors, windows) are for later parts.
Render tiles and mcd fit were not looked at or run.

summary: Roofs: ["parts/roofs.mjs builds the main roofs of plots 0-3, the store and the coop with the roof tool (one roof() call each, explicit palette mixes), plus hand-built porch shed roofs at z 6..8 (store at y 7).", "make.sh gives a whole build.nbt. summary:
Fittings: P3 fittings built in parts/fittings.mjs: 245 blocks, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks. It covers doors (both halves), glazed windows, shutters, porch posts/rails/steps for plots 0-3 and 7, the store's door transom and shop windows, and the white-on-black STORE banner with the MILL CO board.
Build.nbt is whole (make.sh ran clean); `mcd check` walks end to end, `mcd fit` reports only the coop shutters (P5) and a banner false positive. Plan checklist ticked and elements 6, 11, 12, 13, 30 marked in elements.md.
Deviations: STORE letters are white on black_wall_banner (palette has no white banner); the MILL CO board is oak with no chains (palette has no chain id); store_sign is a local helper, not vocab's.
polish: Coop shutters at plan (64,2,12) and (67,3,12) float: the coop() helper's chicken door and vent sit on air (P5 yards / coop owner).
Store cornice ends at 85,14,8 and 94,14,8 (file coords) are orphan dark_oak_stairs from the shell's false_front; shell owner should check.
`mcd fit` flags the STORE wall banners as floating; they are wall banners on the false front, so this looks like a fit false positive, not a real fault. Not confirmed beyond the zoom render.
Porch roofs, porch lanterns (store x86/x93 at z8, y6) and porch-roof signboard support are not built here (P2 roofs / P6 lights).
The STORE letters are white on black, not the plan's black on white, because the palette has no white banner. Adding white_wall_banner to the store palette would restore the plan's look.

waste.tool: bannerWord/signboard options that take palette-checked materials, or a palette-aware sign helper that picks ids from palette.json.

Give them the porch posts, rails and steps for plots 0-3 and 7 to set out and check against the shell's deck and piers, so posts and rails are checked against the wall, not only the plan.
Give them the STORE banner and MILL CO board to set against the false front and porch roof, and to choose a white or black board from the store palette before the sign is hung.

summary:

make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; Hearths line: 249 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check shows no floating blocks in my cells; fit flags none in my cells.
Zoom render shows the four stacks reading as chimneys with signal fires; roofs are not in this copy yet, so the roof-through-stack join is unverified.
polish: Roof join unverified: Roofs part is empty in this copy (no roof.json), so I could not check that the roof stays whole around each stack or that the stacks rise 2+ blocks above the roof surface.
Stoves for plots 0 and 3 sit one wall off their chimney (x8 and x39 are the wall between), as the RESERVED cells say; no flue runs through that wall. A stove flue would need a plan change.

fit reports for the other parts, not mine: floating open trapdoor shutters at (64,5,12) and (67,6,12) on the coop, and a hallway to nowhere at P2 hall (27,3,10). check reports 4 orphan blocks at (15,8,9), (20,8,9), (85,14,8), (94,14,8). None are in my cells.

waste.tool: A helper that takes a room box and a chimney box and returns the stove cell and facing (or a table of stove and chimney pairs in base.mjs). vocab's stove() also only does smoker, so the furnace in plot 2 needed a raw g.set.

Check the stack-through-roof join once Roofs lands: the flashing and the cut around each stack so the roof stays whole.

summary:

make.sh leaves a whole build.nbt; the Yards line reports 454 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. plan.md checklist ticked and the built elements recorded in its Notes; elements.md has no tick column, so it is unchanged.
Checked with check, fit and an aerial zoom of the well and garden. The bench armrests are fence posts, not the vocabulary's trapdoors, because fit flagged the trapdoors as floating.
polish: Coop body, nest row, chicken door, keeper door and vent are the shell's coop() output, not this part; element 23 is only partly mine (run, ramp, troughs).
Plot 0 back step is oak stairs at y1 on z18, but the back door threshold is y3 on z17, so the step does not reach the door. The door step belongs to fittings; check the step height there.
Wash-line sheets hang under the y4 rail, so `check` reports them as orphans. This is by design.
walk says P1, P2 and P3 rooms are unreachable because the doors are not built yet (fittings is a stub here). The yards do not block the lane or the back routes.
fit still flags 2 floating shutters on the coop (shell) and a hallway to nowhere in P2 (not this part).
elements.md has no status column, so ticks were recorded in plan.md Notes instead.

summary:
Lane and lights: P6 lane and lights built in parts/lane.mjs: lane strip (y0, x 0..95, z 0..4), nine lamp posts at z 4 with standing lanterns, every plot's side and back fences, picket line with gates (well yard gap 77..78 open), well-yard open side paths, and porch lanterns at y 6, z 8.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with my part (888 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette); the zoom render shows the lane, lamp posts and picket gate reading correctly.
Porch lanterns are skipped in this copy because the roof blocks above them (P2) are not in yet, so they only appear in the merged build.
polish: Porch lanterns (plots 0-3 at x 4,7 / 14,21 / 28,31 / 40,43, and store 86,93, all y 6 z 8) are conditional on a roof block at y 7 above; none were placed in this copy because P2 roofs is a stub here. Verify them in the merged build with mcd fit.

Side and back fences of plots 4, 5 and 7 (garden, coop run, store) and the garden gate overlap P5 Yards' fence ring. Writes are air-only, so whichever part lands first wins; if Yards builds the ring, my copies skip, and the fence states of its cells are not re-linked.
Plot 1 gate uses birch_fence_gate, not spruce_fence_gate, to match the birch pickets on all four houses. Change gate wood in PLOTS if the duplex should differ.
The walk verdict is ok:false in this copy only because the room parts are stubs; the lane and gates do not block any door or path (walkable end to end, min clear width 19).

waste.cost: about 40 lines of local linking code and one extra pass over ~220 fence cells, with a retry from a sed that broke the pass
waste.tool: A build-library or vocab helper like fence_run(g, cells) that links every fence and fence gate (east/west only) against the whole grid, not just its own run.

waste.cost: about 8 hand-written plot rows plus the gap arithmetic (12i+5..6, the well's 77..78)
waste.tool: A plan.json-driven plot table (per-plot wood, gate x, gap x, back line) that the lane and yard parts both read, so the grid is written once.

waste.cost: one zoom render and a guess at the air cells under the shed roof
waste.tool: mcd room or a lantern-spot finder for exterior porches (air at y 6 with a block above at y 7), so it can run on the merged build instead of guessing.

waste.what: Ticked plan.md and elements.md by hand and wrote the NOTES line.
waste.cost: three Read and three Edit calls on two shared files

companions.task: Place and check the porch lanterns under each roof (y 6, z 8) and confirm the lamp posts on the lane edge read as a lit row from the street.
Lay out the well yard's open dirt_path sides and the picket gap, and confirm the ground patches (grass, coarse dirt, rooted dirt) meet the lane edge cleanly.
Own the fence line for every plot: post and rail joins, gate hangs and corners across the neighbouring plots, so the fences are linked once in one place and not by each part.

summary:
room: P0 front room: P0 front room furnished inside [4,3,10,7,6,12]: birch table (fence post + top slab) with two birch stair chairs, a lit west-facing smoker by the east chimney at (7,3,12), a barrel dresser with a potted poppy, and a lit candle on the table. Paths stay clear from the front door (x5..6) to the partition door (x5, z13).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the room line shows 9 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE. The room check shows min light 9 with 0 dark cells and fit OK; the walk is UNREACHABLE only because the front steps, door and porch rails (Fittings) are still stubs.
Source is parts/room-1.mjs, layers() draws it; room.png was read and the table, chairs and smoker read as a living room.
polish: Walkability not verified by the tool: `$MCD room` reports UNREACHABLE because the front door, step and porch rails from Fittings are not built yet. By reading the grid, x5..6 at z10..12 and x5 at z13 are clear, and the table, chairs, barrel and smoker are each reachable from an adjacent clear cell. Re-run `$MCD room` after Fittings lands to confirm OK.

Lighting: the spec asked for a lantern hung from the plate, but I used a lit candle on the table. A hanging lantern needs a block above it at y7 inside the room, and the roof part is still a stub, so I could not confirm one. Light is already min 9 with the lit smoker (13) and the candle, so a lantern is optional. If the roof leaves y7 solid, hang one at (5,6,11) from iron_chain.
Floor: the spec said birch-plank floor, but the shell's floor deck is oak_planks at y2, outside my box, so I did not change it. Birch would need a shell change or a carpet on top.
Smoker at (7,3,12) is also in the Hearths stove list (RESERVED). If Hearths places it first, my write is refused by runParts. That is harmless, but Hearths should keep the same state (west, lit).
Plan.md checklist and elements.md have no room-level ticks, so nothing was ticked. I did not edit shared files, to avoid racing the parallel workers.

waste.what: Drew the furniture as three layers of 4-character rows and worked out each chair's facing and each slab/fence stacking by hand, cell by cell.
waste.cost: About 6 cell decisions and 2 rebuild cycles; the rows were written once and only the lighting was retried.
waste.tool: A room-furnishing helper that takes a named layout (focal piece, table with N chairs, dresser against a wall) and emits the layers() text with facings and stacking already correct.

waste.what: Checked each block id against palette.json by reading the file and grepping roles, instead of running `$MCD blocks --check` on the list.
waste.cost: About 8 ids checked by eye, with one grep.
waste.tool: `$MCD palette-check <room.json>` or a palette-aware layers() that refuses off-palette ids before the build.

waste.what: Could not confirm the walk verdict; the only check was reading the grid, because the door and steps come from Fittings.
waste.cost: One extra room check run, and a manual reachability read of the floor grid.
waste.tool: `$MCD room --assume-open-doors` (or a walk from the room's own openings) so a room can be verified before the shell's entry parts land.

waste.what: Decided on the candle-versus-lantern lighting by reasoning about whether the y7 ceiling is solid; no tool reports what is above the room.
waste.cost: Two lamp options considered, no build test.
waste.tool: `$MCD room` lamp suggestions should list which hanging anchors (blocks at y+1) actually exist in the current build.

companions.task: Decide the hanging lantern from the head plate once the roof part shows whether y7 above the room is solid, and check that the light map still reads 8+ with the candle removed.
Build the table and the two chairs as proper joinery from the same birch stock as the walls, so the chairs' back and seat faces are right the first time.
Lay a white_carpet rug under the table between the chairs and the door path, which would give the front room its focal ground.

summary:
room: P0 back room: P0 back room is furnished as a shotgun bedroom in parts/room-2.mjs: red bed (head west at x4, foot x5, z15) with a bedside fence and standing lantern, a two-chest dresser on the east wall with a lit candle and a potted poppy, and a white carpet between the chests. make.sh placed 9 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines.
Checks: the walk from the partition door (5,6,14) reaches 12 of 12 floor cells including the back-door column, every floor cell is lit (min 10, 0 dark), and fit is OK. The eye view from the partition door reads as a bedroom (tiles/P0-back-room-from-the-partition-door.png).
The official rooms.json check still says NEEDS WORK because its entrance is the store and the front room, door and gate are stubs.
polish: Official `mcd room` with rooms.json reports UNREACHABLE (0 of 7 cells): its entrance [89,1,5] is in the store and the P0 front room, front door and lane gate are still stubs. From the partition door [5,6,14] it is OK (12/12 reachable), so the furniture is fine once those parts land.

rooms.json y convention is unclear: the box y3..6 makes the room tool see only 7 of the 12 floor cells, and the floor is reported at y=6. The file's floor cells are y6 (plan y3, file offset +3). The orchestrator should confirm whether rooms.json boxes are file or plan coordinates.
The plan's bed footprint says x4..5 z15..16. I used z15 only, with the bedside lamp at x4 z16, so z16 is not a bed cell.
plan.md's checklist has no line for room parts, so I did not tick anything there.

waste.what: Worked out the furniture cell by cell from the room's text plan, then checked it again by hand after the first room check reported the room unreachable.
waste.cost: about 4 layout and coordinate passes, plus one wrong-coordinate retry because the room tool's y convention (file vs plan) was not obvious
waste.tool: A `mcd room --entrance-at-door <room>` option (or a rooms.json flag that auto-picks the room's own doorway as the entrance) would test walkability inside a room before the front parts exist. The tool should also state which y frame rooms.json boxes use.

waste.what: Chose the bed's facing and the head/foot cells by hand, then confirmed them with the eye render.
waste.cost: 2 render passes
waste.tool: A `bed` placement check in `mcd fit` or the room tool that reports which wall the head touches and which way it faces would have settled this in one step.

companions.task: Build the dresser so it reads as furniture and not a pair of chests: a plank frame with drawer fronts, a proper top, and the chest hardware turned to face the room.
Check the one lantern and candle against the bedroom's dark corners, and confirm the bed's head stays in the lamp's glow. I placed the light by hand from the room tool's readout.

summary:
room: P1 west flat: P1 west flat furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: a central spine (x15) kept clear from the door to the back, with a spruce table and chairs, a stove by the chimney, a red bed at x14 z14..15, and barrels, chest and lanterns on the east side.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; room check: 7/7 floor cells reachable and min light 12, with no dark cells, FIT OK.
Standalone the walk reports "no way in" because the porch step at [15,1,6] is Fittings' job; with a scratch step added, the room check is OK.
polish: Walkability depends on the Fittings part building the porch step: spruce_stairs facing south at x15 y1 z6 (plan: step in each gap). Without it the walk reports 'no way in'; with it (tested on a scratch copy) all cells are reachable and OK.
The party-wall chimney cells x17 z12..13 are still air until P4 builds the chimney, so the walk plan shows them as doorways 'D'. Not my cells; they clear once the chimney exists.

elements.md items 19 (beds) and 20 (tables) are only partly built: this room has one bed (bed() at x14 z14..15) and one table (spruce_fence + spruce_slab top at x14 z12). I did not tick them: they are cross-room items, plan.md has no room checklist, and I did not edit shared files.
Room look: room.png is small, and the table and chairs are hard to read from above. Visually acceptable, but a larger inside-eye view would confirm the focal read.

waste.cost: about 3 layout iterations in head, 0 tool runs
waste.tool: a `mcd room --layout <file>` dry run that takes a layers() legend and rows and reports walk and light before make.sh, so a layout is tested without a full rebuild
